en.title: Maximum Number of Beautiful Substrings
en.description:
The string contains only lowercase letters and dots; each dot can be replaced with any lowercase letter. A beautiful substring is a contiguous substring whose characters are all the same. Find the maximum total number of beautiful substrings after the replacements.

The source problem's rules and examples are clear; this site adds the input character set, the length limit, and stdin/stdout.

Source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/fortinet#5-maximize-beautiful-substrings (fixed statement fingerprint 2366a16fa69aa08412d60bb37be054bfb4cf09f2cbc7ca7767d9c8edc5757273). The input/output protocol and bounds added by this site follow the statement and are not claimed to be rules of the original site.
en.input: A single line containing the string color (1≤length≤2000), whose characters are only a-z or . (dot).
en.output: Output the maximum number of beautiful substrings.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the full approach, proof, and complexity.
hints: Count each fixed-character segment on its own, and fill each dot segment with a single character. If the fixed segments on both sides have the same character, merge them; otherwise merge the whole dot segment into the side with the larger gain.
